plant.compliance: All cycads, including Cycas revoluta, are listed on CITES Appendix II, so international trade needs permits; check that nursery-propagated stock is documented.
plant.foliage: evergreen; stiff, glossy, pinnate dark green fronds with sharp-tipped leaflets
plant.hardinessNote: Tender: needs frost-free protection under glass or indoors in winter, minimum about 1 to 5°C.
plant.pollination: not applicable; a dioecious cycad that bears cones rather than flowers, grown for foliage
plant.prune: Remove dead or yellowed fronds at the base with secateurs. Wear gloves, as the leaflet tips are sharp.
plant.resilience: Tolerates dry air and short dry spells; damaged by frost and cold wet compost. Pests: scale insects and mealybugs, especially indoors.

plant.toxicity: Highly toxic: all parts, especially the seeds, can be fatal if eaten, causing liver failure. Children, dogs and cats are at risk, and dogs are frequently poisoned.
uncertain: hardiness: given as H2 from memory of the RHS profile, but not confident. Some sources give brief tolerance of about -5 to -7°C when dry, which could suggest H3. Verify the RHS band online.
hardinessNote: the °C range follows the H2 assumption and must change if the band is corrected.
height/spread: the ultimate size in UK cultivation is estimated; plants grow extremely slowly and in pots usually stay well under 1 m for many years.
cvs: no widely sold UK cultivars known with confidence, so left blank.
rootSize: not known, so left blank.
sunMin: a judgement; it tolerates bright indirect light indoors but not shade.
clay: judged 'no' because it needs sharp drainage. This is not a documented test.
compliance: the CITES Appendix II listing for all Cycadaceae is remembered and should be confirmed. No plant passport or breeders' rights issues are known.
plant.uses: Conservatory · houseplant · patio pots moved under cover for winter · exotic summer displays
plant.visual: Rosette of stiff glossy dark green feather-like fronds on a stout shaggy trunk · year-round foliage · very slow
plant.water: Water when the top of the compost dries in summer; keep almost dry in winter, never letting water sit in the crown.
